basics.name: Korin Eckstrom
basics.label: Bioinformatics Engineer
basics.summary: Experienced bioinformatician with a demonstrated history of working in both the biotech/pharma industry & academic settings. Experience developing workflows in multiple languages, statistical analysis and visualization with R & Python, and processing multi-modal omics data including Whole Exome and Genome Sequencing, Metagenomics, single-cell and bulk RNA-seq, and more with data from major platforms including Illumina, Oxford Nanopore, and PacBio.

work.name: Genentech
work.summary: Bioinformatician within Early Research & Development. Maintained & developed production level workflows for analysis of clinical, preclinical, and safety assessment data. Involved in cloud migration & framework, benchmarking of new tools and workflows, and development of visualization applications.
highlights: Programming languages: R, Python, Shiny, Bash, SQL

Development Practices & Tools: Git, CI/CD, Containers (Docker, Singularity, Podman), Semantic
Versioning, RESTful APIs, FastAPI, Jira
Cloud Computing: AWS Batch & Omics, ECR, Step & Lambda functions, IAM roles, s3 Storage
Data-centric: Wrangling, Transformation (ETL), Visualization, and Cataloging

work.name: University of Vermont, Larner College of Medicine
work.summary: Member of the Bioinformatics Shared Resource branch of VIGR and Colgate Labs within the Larner College of Medicine, serving stakeholders in colleges across the university at large. Responsible for assisting in design, data management & delivery, and analysis for customers of the VIGR core facility, partners at numerous medical centers, and Vermont state entities. Assistant instructor in courses taught by VIGR faculty, including MMG 231 and 232.
highlights: Pipeline development & processing of metagenomics, transcriptomics, structural variants, and other assays to meet user needs

courses: Thesis: Evaluating The Resistome And Microbial Composition During Food Waste Feeding And Composting On A Vermont Poultry Farm
